items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Analysis of the Third Circuit's Sept. 29 ruling that ROSS's unlicensed copying of Westlaw headnotes to train an AI legal-search tool was not fair use; argues the more an AI is marketed as solving research tasks, the less transformative it is for STM content, and that an emerging AI-licensing market weighs against fair use.

items.title: Just-in-Time Synthesis: A New Approach to an Old Genre
items.excerpt: Compares commissioned review articles with AI-generated, question-time overviews (e.g. Elsevier's LeapSpace, publishers wiring content to assistants via MCP), asking how readers can tell enough about how a synthesis was made to trust it.

items.title: The Anatomy of "Harm": An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses the federation's study detailing the harm generative AI causes publishers and authors and what reproduction-rights organisations want from licensing and policy.

items.title: New analysis finds no evidence of racial bias in Pangram
items.excerpt: After Esquire's piece on AI-writing accusations against Black writers, a new analysis finds no evidence that cultural differences in writing style trigger Pangram false positives, though it doesn't rule out racism in how accusations are made.

items.title: Pangram Isn't Racist
items.excerpt: AI-writing researcher Tuhin Chakrabarty runs the numbers on whether the Pangram AI detector disproportionately flags Black writers' prose, concluding the data do not show racial bias.

items.title: The Department of Justice Is Using AI Detector Pangram Against Defense Attorneys
items.excerpt: Federal prosecutors are running defense filings through the Pangram AI-text detector and citing the results in court, extending AI-writing detection from publishing and classrooms into litigation.

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: ALTA and 11 other creative organisations filed an amicus brief in Authors Guild v. OpenAI/Microsoft arguing AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of LLM outputs' and that translations deserve copyright protection. (Amicus follow-up; no ruling yet.)

items.title: Can this golden audio era deliver on its potential?
items.excerpt: Audio executives from Audible, Storytel, ElevenLabs, Bookwire, Legimi and Planeta weigh AI narration and translation: Storytel says 'AI makes it possible for every book to have a voice', ElevenLabs cites a Michael Caine voice-replica Odyssey, while narrators warn ACX is swamped by AI and scammers.

items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Opinion: Marian Stan argues AI tools now give aspiring novelists the editorial feedback they have long struggled to get from a contracting publishing industry.

items.title: Cambridge Dictionary names 'human' Word of the Year 2026
items.excerpt: Cambridge Dictionary picked 'human' as its 2026 Word of the Year for a year 'defined by global debates on what it means to be human when AI is blurring the boundaries between people and machines'.

items.title: Oxford Word of the Year 2026 shortlist: slopaganda, microdrama, doomerism, post-literate
items.excerpt: Oxford University Press's 2026 Word of the Year shortlist includes 'slopaganda' (AI-generated propaganda slop) and 'post-literate', reflecting AI's effect on reading and language.

items.title: Wizards of the Coast shares AI copyright settlement money with D&D's authors
items.excerpt: Wizards of the Coast, which filed Bartz v. Anthropic claims as copyright owner of D&D novels and modules, says it will pass its share of the $1.5bn settlement (about $3,000 per book) to the writers who created those works.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Publisher Arrested Over AI-Generated Books With Fake Authors Supplied to Public Libraries
items.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's anti-corruption directorate arrested Chennai publisher R Mohan (Agal Vilakku, Phoenix Publications) over a Rs 1.74 crore library supply of books allegedly carrying fictitious authors, AI-generated and web-lifted content, dubious ISBNs and invented history.

items.title: Over 500 million Claude tokens help explain 1,000 years of Persian poetry
items.excerpt: Toronto engineer Arman Nejad used Claude to write modern-Persian explanations for more than 1.6 million couplets by all 245 poets in the Ganjoor archive, from Rudaki to Shahriar, now live on Ganjoor and in its public data repo.

items.title: Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza on weathering the AI controversy and reclaiming his Caine Prize moment
items.excerpt: After an AI detector flag reported by The Atlantic triggered a review, the Caine Prize found on Nov 11 'no evidence' his winning story used generative AI and reaffirmed the award; the Zimbabwean writer speaks about the ordeal.

items.title: Author Says the Hundreds of Romance Novels She Publishes Every Year Are Fine Because They Use Many LLMs
items.excerpt: South African writer Coral Hart has published about 370 romance novels since February 2025 under 10+ pen names using ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, defending the output's quality because it draws on multiple models.

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: Long read: BookBub survey finds 45% of authors use generative AI; a Stony Brook study finds 1 in 5 Amazon self-published genre novels contain over 25% AI text; Hachette pulled US release of 'Shy Girl' over AI suspicions.

items.title: Taylor & Francis Retracts Paper Over Hidden AI Prompt Injection
items.excerpt: Taylor & Francis retracted a biomechanics paper after sleuths found hidden prompt-injection text designed to manipulate AI-assisted peer-review tools.

items.title: 책 속 지식, AI 학습데이터로…셀렉트스타, 출판업계와 협력
items.excerpt: 셀렉트스타가 대한출판문화협회와 AI 학습용 출판데이터 공급 기술협력 MOU를 맺고, 출판사 콘텐츠를 저작권을 보호하면서 AI 학습용으로 가공·품질 검증하는 체계를 구축한다. (Korean licensing follow-up.)

items.title: 비플릭스, AI 기술로 웹툰에 움직임 더한 '무빙툰' 출시
items.excerpt: 국내 OTT 비플릭스가 AI로 정지된 웹툰 컷마다 움직임을 입힌 '무빙툰' 서비스를 모바일·PC 웹에 출시했다. 다른 웹툰 서비스에도 적용 가능한 기술이라고 밝혔다.

items.title: Namoo - 부모님의 이야기를 AI 인터뷰로 기록해 이북과 오디오북으로 만들어 주는 앱
items.excerpt: AI가 인터뷰어가 되어 부모님에게 음성으로 질문하고, 답변을 챕터 단위로 정리해 전자책과 오디오북으로 만들어 주는 회고록 앱 Namoo가 출시됐다(대필 작가 대체형 AI 메모아).

items.title: 리트 만점자 AI 부정행위 의혹에…출간 도서 환불 요구 빗발
items.excerpt: LEET 만점자 이진우씨의 AI 활용 부정행위 의혹이 확산하면서 그가 쓴 베스트셀러 자기계발서 '브레인 악셀'에 대한 환불 요구가 교보문고 등 서점가에 잇따르고 있다.

items.title: "AI 저작권 규제해도, 안 해도 문제"... 세계 도서관계, 법적 공백·과잉 규제 동시 경고
items.excerpt: 국제도서관협회연맹(IFLA)이 각국 생성형 AI 저작권 입법현황을 조사해, 과잉 규제와 법적 공백 모두가 도서관의 연구지원·지식 접근을 위협한다며 명확한 지침을 촉구했다.

items.title: AI could bring books to radio, but broadcasters still need to direct the story
items.excerpt: Synthetic voices could let radio stations test serialised literary readings and narrated essays, but success depends on editorial judgement, rights clearance and listener trust.
